release.title: Day trips, and activities that know their stay
release.summary: Plan day trips that leave your stay and come back the same day, see them on the map with their own route, and add activities from one tidy button.

items.text: 🧭 Plan day trips: mark an outing like Sintra from Lisbon as a day trip and it gets its own marker and a dashed route out and back on the map.
🏨 Every activity now belongs to a stay, and you can move it to another stay and day right from its details.
✨ New AI-planned trips suggest day trips from your bases instead of squeezing them in as extra stops.
💬 The trip assistant can add, change and remove day trips for you, with ready-made day-trip prompts in its / menu that follow what you have selected.
🔗 Select a day trip or its stay in the calendar and a dashed line shows where it leaves from; day trips also carry their stay's colour.
➕ The calendar's activities row has a single add button, like stays and transfers, and starts on the stay you have selected.
🔁 A day trip can end in a different stay when your plans need it, tucked away under more options.
🗺️ Example trips now show their classic day trips on the map, and the Portugal road trip visits Sintra as a day trip from Lisbon.
Added optional `stayCityId`, `activityKind` and `dayTripReturnCityId` item fields with one shared stay resolver, replacing three date-window copies.
Added a top-level `dayTrips` list to the itinerary schemas and prompts, a forgiving preparation step, and one shared placement builder for the worker, client and benchmark parsers.
The AI benchmark reports day-trip counts and downgraded day trips as non-blocking checks.
Trip Agent schemas accept stay and day-trip fields plus the location resolver's provenance fields; unknown city references are rejected with a fixable hint.
Documented the model and every affected surface in `docs/ACTIVITIES_AND_DAY_TRIPS.md`.
